abstract: This paper investigates whether right-wing digital news sites in Europe and the United States form an interconnected, transnational information ecology. Using hyperlink networks, it examines how such sites reference one another within and across national borders, and identifies additional websites that function as shared transnational reference points. The study situates this analysis within the broader emergence of an alternative digital news infrastructure that accompanies a more transnationally networked political right.
key_claims: The rise of a transnationally networked political right in Europe and the US coincides with an emerging alternative digital news infrastructure.
Right-wing digital news sites are interconnected both within and across countries through hyperlink networks.
Certain shared reference sites serve as common nodes connecting right-wing news ecologies across national boundaries.
Hyperlinking helps circulate information and establish shared epistemologies among right-wing audiences transnationally.
methods: Hyperlink network analysis of right-wing digital news sites.
Comparative approach spanning multiple European countries and the United States.
Mapping of interconnections within countries and across borders, and identification of transnationally shared reference points.
findings: Right-wing digital news sites exhibit interconnection at both national and transnational levels (specific figures not available from the abstract).
Some external sites act as commonly shared transnational reference points within the right-wing news ecology.
contributions: Provides empirical mapping of the transnational structure of right-wing alternative news infrastructures.
Advances understanding of how shared epistemologies and information flows form across national right-wing media environments.
Extends comparative research on alternative/right-wing media into a cross-national, network-analytic framework.
framing: The paper is positioned within research on alternative digital news media, political communication, and the transnationalization of the political right, framing hyperlink networks as infrastructure through which shared epistemologies and information circulation are established.
